items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Milan, that man's name was Hank Milan, he was the proprietor of that club... And Hank tried to get us to stay.

ctx.x: And so you were telling me after Pearl Harbor you drove back and there was a blackout, a blackout being when they just pulled the plug. There were no lights.

Oh, that was the worst feeling. I shall never forget that feeling. That experience was something. That's another thing. There have been many things, several things that I've talked about that were things that I should never forget, but I can remember this just as if it happened yesterday almost, because naturally earlier in the day you heard this thing about the Pearl Harbor situation, you know, and in the meantime the proprietor of this club was trying to get the band to stay. He was trying to get us to stay in…

back down here. And the war has broken out now," and I says -- because, you know, my son was a very little fellow, a very young child. And I said, "No, I'm going to be home. I want to be home with my child." Because my husband and I had separated, incidentally, at that time, too, and in fact I was in the process of getting my divorce from him. And I said, "No, I'm not coming back to San Diego, so get somebody else." So then Dootsie Williams -- nobody wanted to stay. They did not want to stay. So that's how we --…
